pension.system: ERSRI (Employees' Retirement System of Rhode Island), administered by the Office of the General Treasurer / Retirement Board

plans.benefit_formula: Hybrid: defined benefit + mandatory defined contribution. DB accrual 1% of final average compensation per year for service after July 1, 2012 (members with 20+ years as of 6/30/2012 accrue 2% per year after July 1, 2015). Final average comp = highest 3 consecutive years for retirements on/after July 1, 2024 (was 5). Caps: 80% (Schedule A) / 75% (Schedule B). DC plan: employee 5%, employer 1.0%-1.5% depending on service as of 6/30/2012 (0% for those with 20+ years).
plans.employee_contribution: DB 3.75% of pay (11% for members with 20+ years as of 6/30/2012) plus DC 5% (total 8.75% for most). Certain public-safety titles (deputy sheriffs, capitol/environmental police, state fire marshal staff, campus police) 10% effective Jan 1, 2025.
plans.retirement_age: Social Security normal retirement age with 5 years of service (proportional transition for pre-2012 members, floor age 59), or Rule of 95 at age 62+ (also 65/30, 64/31, 63/32, 62/33). Early retirement with 20+ years up to 5 years early with reductions. 5-year vesting.
plans.cola: Full COLA suspended for post-6/30/2012 retirees until aggregate funded ratio exceeds 75% (lowered from 80% in 2024). Meanwhile, 25% of the computed COLA is paid annually (2023 law). COLA = 50% (5-yr avg return minus 5.5%, 0-4%) + 50% CPI (max 3%), capped 3.5%, applied to first ~$25,855 of benefit (indexed; $31,026 base for 7/2012-6/2015 retirees). Pre-July 2012 retirees exempt from funding test. FY2027 post-retirement increase base per GRS: $32,559 limit in 2027.

retiree_health.summary: State employees retiring after Sept 30, 2008 with 20+ years of service and age 59+ get an 80% State subsidy; retiree pays 20% of the plan's actual cost. Under 20 years: retiree pays 100%. Retire before 59 with 20+ years: subsidy starts at 59. Pre-65: self-insured BCBSRI plan. 65+: must enroll in Medicare A and B; State deposits subsidy (percent of age-based Plan F benchmark) into a health reimbursement arrangement for a Medigap/Medicare Advantage plan bought through Via Benefits. State Police retirees keep active coverage at their retirement co-share until 65. Judges and legislators may buy coverage at group rates. Prefunded through an OPEB trust since FY2011. OPEB valuation 6/30/2025 (GRS), state employees group: AAL $684.2M, actuarial assets $473.2M, UAAL $210.9M, funded 69%, 7,697 retirees/beneficiaries, 11,113 actives; FY2028 ADEC $40.97M (3.86% of payroll). State Police OPEB 109% funded; FY2028 rate 17.39%. Total FY2028 ADEC all groups $50.3M. Employer retiree-health rate in FY2027 budget: 3.08% of salary for regular state employees (FY2026R 3.25%).

jobs.Housekeeper: Cleans and maintains buildings at a state college or university campus (URI, RIC or CCRI). The work covers offices, classrooms, residence halls, bathrooms and other spaces, following daily custodial standards.
jobs.Eligibility Technician I: Works mostly at the Department of Human Services deciding whether people qualify for public benefit programs, both when they first apply and at renewal. They interview applicants, collect proof and process applications through to approval or denial.
jobs.Cook S Helper: Assists cooks and food service supervisors in a state institution kitchen, such as a hospital or residential facility. Duties are simple food preparation, serving and dishwashing work under close supervision.
jobs.Community Living Aide: Provides daily care to people with intellectual and developmental disabilities living in state-run community group homes (under BHDDH). The job mixes personal care, carrying out treatment plans and running the household, including cooking and cleaning.
jobs.Deputy Sheriff: Provides security in the state's courthouses and moves prisoners between courts, prisons, jails and hospitals. Deputies also handle extraditions and serve civil and criminal court papers.
jobs.Programming Services Officer: A mid-to-senior administrator who runs a program for a department or division head, managing how its services are delivered to employees or the public. They analyze operations, write reports and recommendations, and coordinate the work of program units.
jobs.Seasonal State Lifeguard: A summer lifeguard at a state beach run by DEM. They watch the water and beach, enforce rules and respond to water emergencies and injuries.
jobs.Inst Attndnt Psychiatric: Gives hands-on daily care to patients with severe, chronic mental illness in a state psychiatric hospital, following nursing and treatment plans. They also supervise patients and keep the unit safe.
jobs.Prob Parol Officer Ii: Supervises adults on probation or parole in the community for the Department of Corrections, working with the courts and the Parole Board. They investigate, assess and counsel offenders and enforce the conditions of their release.
jobs.Park Ranger Ii: A seasonal ranger who patrols and protects a particular state park or beach, helping visitors and guarding against accidents, fire, theft and trespass.
jobs.Interdepartmental Project Mgr: A senior manager who works across state agencies to coordinate and integrate human services programs. They run special projects, do policy and fiscal analysis, and represent several departments to officials and the media.
jobs.Chief Implementation Aide: A senior staff aide to a high-level official (such as in the Governor's office or a department head's office) who handles the most complex administrative work on major statewide projects. The job includes research, reports, managing official files and public relations writing.
jobs.Highway Maintenance Operator I: A RIDOT road crew member who does physical labor and runs equipment to maintain highways. Work includes pavement and drainage repair, roadside upkeep, signs, and plowing and treating roads in snow and ice.
jobs.Higher Education Admin Asst Ii: An administrative assistant in an academic department at a state college or university. They answer requests, handle office systems and serve as a lead administrative worker, including some budget support.
jobs.Registered Nurse B: A professional nurse in a state hospital, inpatient or community facility (such as Eleanor Slater Hospital or the Veterans Home). At this level they also take charge of patient care and staff when managers are not available, such as on nights or weekends.
jobs.Representative: One of 75 elected members of the Rhode Island House of Representatives, a part-time legislature. Representatives introduce and vote on bills, serve on committees that hold hearings on legislation, and help constituents.
jobs.Certified Nursing Asst Rivh: Gives hands-on daily care to residents of the Rhode Island Veterans Home in Bristol, following nursing care plans. Work includes bathing, moving and monitoring residents and reporting changes to nurses.
jobs.Trooper State Police: A sworn State Police officer who enforces traffic and criminal laws statewide and carries out investigations. Work is on rotating 24/7 shifts and mixes patrol, crash response, arrests and report writing.
jobs.Registered Nurse A: A professional nurse in a state inpatient or community facility. They assess patients, deliver nursing care and treatments, and work with doctors and other members of the care team.
jobs.Child Protective Investigator: Investigates reports of child abuse and neglect for DCYF, often starting with calls to the Child Abuse Hotline. They interview families and others in the field, assess whether children are safe and take action to protect them.
jobs.Administrative Officer: A general administrator who takes complex administrative work off the hands of a department, agency or division head. They study operations, write reports and do public relations and research for their boss.
jobs.Corr Officer Lt: A shift supervisor at the state prison who oversees a group of correctional officers. They assign and review officers' work, set and enforce performance standards, and act as part of the facility's management team.
jobs.Chief Program Development: Leads planning, program development and research for a state department. They identify needs, design new programs, improve existing ones and coordinate plans between the director and division heads.
jobs.Spec Asst Attorney General: An attorney in the Attorney General's office. Because Rhode Island has no district attorneys, the AG's lawyers prosecute all felonies and many misdemeanors statewide; others work in the civil division on matters like consumer and environmental protection.
jobs.Cook: Runs the cooking on a shift in a state institution kitchen serving fewer than 100 people, or assists a higher-level cook in a larger kitchen. They plan meal preparation, order food and supervise kitchen helpers.
jobs.Casework Supv Ii: Supervises a unit of DCYF child-welfare caseworkers (Social Caseworker IIs) and support staff. They approve decisions about the safety of children, coach staff on policy and practice, and lead unit meetings.
jobs.Juvenile Program Worker: Works at the Rhode Island Training School, the state's juvenile detention facility, supervising and securing the youth held there. They also help with residents' treatment, education and rehabilitation.
jobs.Mental Health Worker: Provides direct care to severely mentally ill patients in a secure forensic setting at the Rhode Island State Psychiatric Hospital. They support the therapeutic environment while supervising patients and keeping them in custody.
jobs.Benefit Claims Specialist: Works at the Department of Labor and Training on difficult or disputed unemployment and temporary disability insurance claims. They investigate facts, recommend decisions, find overpayments and sometimes represent the department at appeal hearings.
jobs.Senior Emp Trng Interviewer: Works in Department of Labor and Training job centers helping job seekers find work and training, and handling unemployment claims interviews. They match people to job openings, run workshops and do fact-finding with workers and employers.
jobs.Sr Janitor: Cleans and maintains a moderate-sized public building and leads a small crew of janitors, or helps supervise cleaning in a large building.
jobs.Certified Nursing Assistant: Gives hands-on daily care to patients in a state hospital or care facility, following nursing care plans. Work includes bathing, moving and monitoring patients and reporting changes to nurses.
jobs.Customer Svs Repres Iii Dmv: A senior counter clerk at the Division of Motor Vehicles who processes registrations, titles and licenses and collects fees. At this top level they also act as lead worker and help solve harder customer problems.
jobs.Sr Maintenance Technician: A skilled all-round maintenance worker at a state facility who repairs plumbing, steam, electrical and kitchen/laundry equipment. They also do carpentry, masonry, painting and machine shop work.
jobs.Environmental Scientist Ii: A scientist (mainly at the Department of Environmental Management) who does moderately complex technical work on environmental permitting, compliance and pollution prevention programs. They help run projects and write technical plans and documents.
jobs.Senior Trooper State Police: A more senior non-supervisory State Police rank. The State Police publishes a job description only for the entry Trooper role, which covers enforcing traffic and criminal laws and conducting investigations.
jobs.Janitor: Cleans and does simple maintenance in a public building or state institution.
jobs.Park Ranger I: A seasonal ranger at a state park or beach who helps visitors, patrols for rule violations and does maintenance like litter pickup and restroom cleaning.
jobs.Asst Administrative Officer: Handles routine administrative duties for a department, agency or division head and often supervises its clerical and office operations. They gather information and make studies to support decisions.
jobs.Capitol Police Officer: A police officer who protects the State House, state buildings and grounds, and the people in them. They patrol, keep order, control access and make arrests when needed.
jobs.Senator: One of 38 elected members of the Rhode Island Senate, a part-time legislature. Senators introduce and vote on bills, serve on committees that hold hearings on legislation, and help constituents.
jobs.Information Services Tech Ii: Provides information and publication services for a state agency, including web content and printed materials. They answer requests, maintain publication schedules and build web pages.
jobs.Legal Counsel: An attorney who gives legal advice and services to a state department or agency. They also act as hearing officers, draft regulations and represent the agency in court.
jobs.Information Services Tech I: An entry-level information worker who answers phone and in-person questions from the public and agencies and handles publications and data for a state office.
jobs.Sr Human Svs Plcy Sys Spec: An analyst (mostly at human services agencies like DHS) who studies federal and state program rules and writes the policies and procedure manuals that staff follow. They also study proposed new programs and systems.
jobs.Sr Word Processing Typist: A clerical worker who does complex word processing and data entry, producing reports, letters, legal documents and spreadsheets.
jobs.Social Case Worker: A caseworker who provides social services in areas such as public assistance, child welfare, veterans' welfare, medical/psychiatric social work or corrections. They work with individuals and families and with treatment teams.
jobs.Customer Service Aide Dhs: Front-desk and clerical worker in Department of Human Services field offices. They greet and register customers, scan and file documents, and help people use forms and the self-service portal.
jobs.Child Support Technician Dcyf: Supports DCYF social workers mainly by driving children and families to appointments, visits and court, and supervising and observing them along the way. They report what they see to caseworkers.
jobs.Implementation Aide: A staff aide to a high-level state official who handles moderately complex administrative tasks for major statewide projects. They prepare correspondence and documents to carry out the official's decisions and keep official files.
jobs.Admin Financial Management: The top finance manager of a state department, responsible for receiving and spending its money properly. They build the department's budget and capital plan and oversee fiscal operations.
jobs.Court Reporter: A stenographer who takes down word-for-word testimony at hearings before the Workers' Compensation Court and produces transcripts.
jobs.Sr Public Hlth Promotion Splst: A Department of Health staff member who runs public education campaigns to prevent chronic disease, infectious disease and injury. They develop materials and events and help supervise other promotion staff.
jobs.Environmental Scientist I: An entry-level environmental scientist (mainly at DEM) who works on permitting, compliance and pollution prevention programs. Fields include air, waste, water, wetlands and underground storage.
jobs.Engr Tech Iii Const Maint: A RIDOT field inspector on highway construction and maintenance projects. They inspect and document materials and contractor work, estimate progress and help supervise lower-level technicians.
jobs.Clinical Social Worker: A social worker in a hospital or statewide mental health or public health program who works on patients' social, emotional and environmental problems. They do individual and group therapy and are part of a clinical team.
jobs.Supvsg Eligibility Technician: Supervises a team of eligibility technicians who decide who qualifies for public assistance programs, mainly at DHS. They also handle the most complex eligibility cases themselves.
jobs.Highway Maintenance Operatorii: A skilled RIDOT equipment operator who runs heavy construction and maintenance machinery to repair highways and clear snow and ice.
jobs.Associate Justice: A judge on one of the state courts (for example the Superior Court, which hears all felonies and larger civil cases, or the Family Court). Judges hear arraignments, motions, trials and appeals in criminal and civil cases and are appointed for life by the Governor with Senate approval.
jobs.Rehabilitation Counselor: A counselor in the state vocational rehabilitation program who helps people with disabilities prepare for and find work, and who also decides disability insurance claims.
jobs.Eligibility Tech Ii Dhs Lobby: An experienced DHS eligibility worker based in the front office/lobby who handles complex benefit eligibility cases for walk-in, remote and appointment customers.
jobs.Park Ranger Iii: A seasonal ranger shift supervisor who manages rangers and equipment on a shift and handles reports and administrative work for the park manager.
jobs.Senior Tax Auditor Taxation: An auditor in the Division of Taxation who examines the books of individuals, partnerships and corporations, including large multistate companies, to determine what they owe the state. Audits sometimes require out-of-state travel.
jobs.Asst Bus Mgt Off: Helps run the business side of a state department or agency, such as files, personnel records, budgets and purchasing, or runs it for a small agency.
jobs.Environmental Scientist Iii: A senior environmental scientist (mainly at DEM) who helps supervise a section and handles difficult compliance, permitting and pollution prevention issues.
jobs.Health Program Administrator: Runs a program at the Department of Health, overseeing its planning, budget, grants and contracts and making sure laws and regulations are followed.
jobs.Information Aide: Answers questions from the public, officials and employees, working out what information people need and pointing them to the right resources or services.
jobs.Business Management Officer: Manages, or helps manage, the business and non-medical services of a state department, including finance, payroll, personnel, purchasing, food service, housekeeping and maintenance.
jobs.Nat Res Oper Tech I Dem: A maintenance worker for the Department of Environmental Management who keeps parks, beaches and other DEM properties in shape. Work ranges from mowing and trash pickup to carpentry, plumbing and equipment repair.
jobs.Asst Admin Financial Mgmt: The deputy finance manager of a state department, helping manage its funds and budget and supervising business office operations.
jobs.Data Analyst I: A data analyst who handles the full cycle of analytics work for a state agency, from defining requirements and cleaning data to building reports and linking datasets.
jobs.Vocational Rehab Counselor Ii: An experienced counselor in the state's Office of Rehabilitation Services who helps people with disabilities get and keep jobs. They review medical, educational and psychological records to decide eligibility and build employment plans with clients.
jobs.Correctional Offcr Hospital Ii: Despite the title, this is a registered nurse who provides nursing care to inmates at the Adult Correctional Institutions.
jobs.Deputy Chf Of Legal Services: The second-in-command of a department's legal office, directing attorneys who advise the department and often handling its legislative liaison work.
jobs.Chf Strategic Plan Mont Eval: Leads the state's strategic planning unit, connecting statewide planning with the budget and tracking how plans are carried out.
jobs.Engr Tech Ii Const Maint: An entry-level RIDOT engineering technician who helps inspect road and bridge construction and maintenance projects. They document materials, gather data for progress estimates, and do surveying and drafting.
jobs.Chief Of Legal Services: The chief lawyer of a state department or agency, directing its legal staff and advising its officials. They help set policy and oversee drafting of rules, legislation and legal opinions.
jobs.Taxpayer Serv Specialist: Helps people and businesses with their Rhode Island tax returns by phone and in person at the Division of Taxation. They explain obligations and procedures and correct taxpayer records.
jobs.Adult Counselor Corrections: A counselor at the Department of Corrections who works with sentenced adults in individual and group sessions. They build treatment plans and coordinate education, vocational, substance-abuse and re-entry programs.
jobs.Office Manager: Runs the front office for a director or associate director in a large state department. They supervise clerical staff and handle calls, visitors, correspondence and files.
jobs.Groundskeeper: Maintains grounds used for outdoor recreation, such as athletic fields and golf courses. Work includes mowing, seeding, fertilizing and repairing paths and fixtures.
jobs.Asst Dir Financial Cntr Mgmt: A senior finance executive who oversees a department's budget, spending controls, financial planning and program evaluation.
jobs.Sr Case Work Supervisor: A senior supervisor of social work staff covering several offices or a program area, such as public assistance, child welfare or hospital social work.
jobs.Fiscal Clerk: A bookkeeping clerk who keeps the financial records of a state agency. They post transactions, reconcile accounts, handle payroll adjustments and petty cash.
jobs.Senior Legal Counsel: A senior state agency attorney who handles complex legal issues, supervises and trains junior attorneys, and serves as a hearing officer in difficult cases.
jobs.Corr Officer Steward: A correctional officer who runs food service in a prison kitchen, cooking meals and supervising the inmates who work there. They also keep control of knives, tools and other hazardous items.
jobs.Eligibility Technician Iii Dhs: The most senior level of DHS eligibility worker, handling the hardest benefit eligibility cases across all programs and coaching less experienced technicians.
jobs.Trooper First Class: A non-supervisory State Police rank above Trooper. The State Police publishes a job description only for the Trooper role, which covers enforcing traffic and criminal laws and conducting investigations.
jobs.Licensed Practical Nurse: Provides practical nursing care to patients under a doctor or registered nurse in a state facility. They give medications and injections, change dressings and track vital signs.
jobs.Higher Education Admin Ast Iii: A senior administrative assistant in an academic department at a state college or university, handling complex office support, grants paperwork and financial entries.
jobs.Hwy Fld Operations Supvr Rdway: A RIDOT crew boss who directs and works with a roadway maintenance crew. They are in charge of daily operations, vehicles, communications and work-zone safety.
jobs.Law Clerk Judiciary: A lawyer, usually a recent law graduate, who works in a judge's chambers for a court term. They provide legal and administrative support to the judge.
jobs.Fiscal Management Officer: Handles financial management for a state agency, controlling spending and doing specialized budget and accounting work, often supervising fiscal staff.
jobs.Asst Dir Administrative Servic: A senior executive who runs a department's administrative support programs for the director and represents the department to other agencies, the General Assembly and the public.
jobs.Engr Tech Iii Materials: A RIDOT technician who samples and tests construction materials like aggregate, asphalt and steel for highway and bridge projects, and helps supervise lower-level testers.
jobs.Campus Police Officer: A sworn police officer at a state college or university who enforces laws and campus rules, patrols, handles traffic and provides emergency medical help.
jobs.Technical Staff Assistant: Supports faculty and students in a college science lab, skills lab or studio, setting up equipment and teaching students how to use it safely.
jobs.Tech Support Specii Unix Ntwk: An IT systems specialist who installs and maintains servers, networks and operating systems for state government computing.
jobs.Information Tech Proj Mgr Doa: Manages mid-size IT projects for one or more state agencies in the Department of Administration, from defining requirements to vendor selection, testing and launch.
jobs.Revenue Officer I Taxation: An entry-level tax collector in the Division of Taxation who helps go after unpaid taxes and missing returns. They interview taxpayers, review their finances and help set up payment plans or enforcement.
jobs.Customer Svs Repres Ii Dmv: A DMV clerk who processes registrations, titles and licenses, collects fees and helps customers with harder transactions, sometimes as lead worker.
jobs.Assistant Public Defender: A lawyer at the state Public Defender's office who represents people who cannot afford an attorney. Depending on division, they defend adults in criminal and probation cases, juveniles in Family Court, parents in abuse and neglect cases, or handle appeals.
jobs.Food Service Supervisor: Supervises dining room or cafeteria staff at a state facility. They train and schedule workers and check that sanitation standards are met.
jobs.Data Analyst Ii: An experienced state data analyst who takes on special and recurring projects across the full data analytics lifecycle.
jobs.Prin Public Hlth Epidemiologis: A senior Department of Health epidemiologist who leads the most complex work tracking, detecting and preventing disease and injury, often as an expert in one program area.
jobs.Data Control Clerk: Enters and controls data going into and out of computer systems, keeps control logs and makes sure reports come out on time.
jobs.Prin Human Svs Plcy Sys Spec: A senior DHS policy specialist who leads the writing of human services policies and systems and supervises other specialists.
jobs.Park Naturalist: A seasonal educator who leads public programs in state parks about wildlife, natural resources and conservation.
jobs.Environmental Engineer Iii: A senior DEM environmental engineer who handles the most complex engineering reviews and leads project staff on inspections and reviews.
jobs.Tech Support Spec Iii Unix Ntw: A senior state IT specialist who leads a small team managing servers, networks or telecommunications, including diagnosing operating system and hardware failures.
jobs.Supvr Child Protective Invest: Supervises DCYF child protective investigators who look into reports of child abuse and neglect, including in institutions.
jobs.Asst Hlth Program Admin: Helps run a Department of Health program, supervising staff and managing its budget, grants and compliance.
jobs.Coord Employ Trng Pgrms: Coordinates statewide employment and training programs at the Department of Labor and Training, such as services for veterans, youth and people with disabilities.
jobs.Campus Patrol Person: A security patrol officer at the University of Rhode Island who guards buildings and enforces parking and traffic rules.
jobs.Supervising Registered Nurse B: A nursing supervisor in a state hospital who schedules and directs nurses, LPNs and attendants, and takes charge of patient care when administrators are not on site.
jobs.Child Supt Enforce Agent Iii: The senior level of DHS child support agent, handling the hardest cases, including interstate cases, liens and collection problems, and training other agents.
jobs.Human Servs Policy Sys Spec: An analyst who helps plan and develop human services programs, policies and electronic systems on a statewide basis.
jobs.Seasonal Beach Manager: Runs a state beach for the summer, managing lifeguards, clerks, rangers and laborers and overseeing facilities, safety and revenue.
jobs.Seasonal Supervising Lifeguard: A lifeguard supervisor at a major state beach who does lifeguard duties and also sets daily and weekly guard schedules under the beach or park manager.
jobs.Sr Pub Hlth Epidemiologist: A Department of Health epidemiologist who tracks and analyzes chronic and infectious diseases in Rhode Island and helps design prevention efforts.
jobs.Building Grounds Officer: Runs the operations, maintenance, repair and construction program for state buildings assigned by the Division of Facilities Management, supervising facilities staff and contractors.
jobs.Behavioral Hlth Clinician Doc: A mental health counselor at the Department of Corrections who assesses and treats inmates' mental health and social problems.
jobs.Prob Parole Suprvr: Supervises a team of probation and parole officers at the Department of Corrections, training them and overseeing case assignments and casework quality.
jobs.Clerk Secretary: A private secretary to a department director or assistant director, handling meetings, inquiries, correspondence and office routines.
jobs.Executive Assistant: A confidential assistant to a senior administrator, especially on labor relations and personnel matters such as grievances and arbitration.
jobs.Administrator Ii Bhddh: A mid-level manager at the Department of Behavioral Healthcare, Developmental Disabilities and Hospitals who helps run an operation or program, analyzing costs and services to improve them.
jobs.Vocational Rehabi Counselor I: An entry-level vocational rehabilitation counselor who screens people with disabilities for services and helps them set job goals.
jobs.Eligibility Tech Ii Dhs Call C: An experienced DHS eligibility worker in the central call center who handles complex benefit eligibility cases by phone.
jobs.Environ Police Officer I Dem: A DEM law enforcement officer who patrols the state's woods, waters and parks by foot, boat and vehicle, enforcing fish and game, boating and other natural resource laws.
jobs.Construction Mgmt Resident Dot: A RIDOT civil engineer who manages large, multi-year road and bridge construction contracts as the main point of contact for contract compliance.
jobs.Human Resources Analyst I: An entry-level professional in the state's Division of Human Resources who works in an area like classification and pay, hiring and testing, or labor relations.
jobs.Enrollment Services Representa: A clerical staff member in a university's enrollment services office who answers questions on registration, financial aid and billing and processes payments.
jobs.Higher Ed Fin Off Preaudit Clk: Checks payment documents in a college or university's central finance office before money goes out, making sure they are accurate and follow state rules.
jobs.Building Superintendent: Supervises the cleaning, custodial, heating and routine maintenance staff in a major public building such as the State House or a courthouse.
jobs.Prin Pub Hlth Prom Specialist: Leads a public health promotion area at the Department of Health, supervising staff, evaluating programs and managing grants.
jobs.Administrator Iii Bhddh: A senior BHDDH manager responsible for running an operational unit or program, and part of the department's leadership team.
jobs.Supervising Registered Nurse A: A nursing supervisor in a state facility who schedules and assigns nursing staff, makes rounds and reviews care and incident reports.
jobs.Employment And Career Advisor: Works with participants in Rhode Island Works (the state's cash assistance program) to set job goals and track their progress toward employment.
jobs.Child Support Enfrcemnt Agt I: Works in the DHS Office of Child Support Services setting up child support cases: locating parents, establishing paternity, and getting support and medical orders through the courts.
jobs.Nursing Care Evaluator Ii: A nurse inspector with the Department of Health who surveys nursing homes and other health care facilities for licensing and federal certification, and investigates complaints of abuse or neglect.
jobs.Prin Employ Trng Interviewer: A senior Department of Labor and Training counselor who provides employment counseling and helps resolve complex unemployment and disability insurance disputes.
jobs.Higher Education Admin Asst I: An entry-level administrative assistant in an academic department at a state college or university, producing documents, reports and class records.
jobs.Corr Officer Capt: A senior shift commander at a state prison who is responsible for all officers on a shift and may stand in for the associate director.
jobs.Corr Off Hosp Ii Evening: Despite the title, this is a registered nurse providing nursing care to inmates at the Adult Correctional Institutions; the payroll title indicates the evening shift.
jobs.Consultant Public Health Nurse: A Department of Health nurse who advises and trains staff at child care facilities, nursing homes, hospitals and other agencies on nursing and disease prevention.
jobs.Clinical Training Specialist: Plans and delivers training for social service staff (such as DCYF workers) on clinical and social service topics, including the core curriculum for new workers.
jobs.Prin Human Servs Bus Officer: Runs accounting and budget systems for a human services agency and audits municipalities and nonprofits, including nursing homes.
jobs.Public Hlth Promotion Speciali: Develops and presents Department of Health public education programs on topics like smoking, nutrition, fitness, seat belts and immunizations.
jobs.Asst Admin Comm Plan Serv: Helps run a planning and policy office that writes State Plans, policy manuals and program plans for a human services department.

assessment.intro: Rhode Island Hurricane's view of where the state could shrink or restructure, based only on the payroll and budget numbers on this page. These are starting points for a closer look, not proof of waste. Each one shows the strongest argument against it.
method: Payroll years 2015 and 2025 compared (people paid, total pay, overtime), from the state's payroll file.
Managers counted by job title (chief, director, deputy, administrator, manager, supervisor, superintendent). Staff per manager below 4 is top-heavy by most public-sector benchmarks.
Share of staff with a pay rate of $100,000 or more.
FY2027 enacted budget compared with FY2026.
Moves of offices between agencies can make one agency look bigger and another smaller; we flag those where we know of them.

why: Management titles grew about ten times faster than the workforce they manage.
A freeze on new supervisory titles, and folding vacant ones back into front-line jobs, is the broadest cut available without touching services.
items.counter: Some growth reflects reclassifying senior specialists into titles with 'chief' or 'administrator' to keep pay competitive, not new layers of bosses.
items.next: Match each new manager title since 2015 to an actual org chart to separate real layers from pay reclassifications.

items.agency: Executive Office of Health & Human Services
why: The most top-heavy agency in state government by both measures.
Pay grew far faster than headcount.
Almost all of its $4.6 billion is Medicaid passed to providers; the in-house staff is small, so it should be the most streamlined, not the most layered.
items.counter: Running a $4 billion Medicaid program takes scarce finance, actuarial and legal specialists who command high pay.
items.next: Compare EOHHS staffing and pay with Medicaid agencies of similar-size states.

why: Half its staff earn six figures and there are about two workers for every manager.
Its central services (IT, purchasing, HR, facilities) are where consolidation usually saves the most.
items.counter: It runs shared services for every agency; cutting it can push costs back into the departments.
items.next: Break its workforce down by division (Purchasing, Enterprise Technology, HR, Capital Asset Management) to see where the layers are.

why: Overtime is a third of base pay, and correctional officer overtime alone equals about 208 full-time officers.
Turnover is rising fast while nearly half the staff are long-serving, so a retirement wave will make overtime worse.
items.counter: Prison posts must be staffed around the clock by law and contract; cutting positions would raise overtime, not lower it. Per hour, overtime costs about the same as a new hire with benefits.
items.next: Get the post-staffing plan and minimum-staffing rules; the savings are in hiring and retention, not headcount cuts.

why: Staff fell by almost a quarter while overtime stayed heavy and the budget kept rising.
Eleanor Slater Hospital and state-run group homes are the cost drivers.
items.counter: Hospital and group-home care has licensing ratios; fewer staff means more overtime by definition.
items.next: Compare cost per patient-day at Eleanor Slater with private and other-state psychiatric hospitals.

why: The fastest-growing agency on the payroll.
items.counter: Much of the growth likely came from boards and functions moved into it from elsewhere, plus new duties such as cannabis and building-code work.
items.next: Separate transferred staff from new hires before judging.

numbers: Human Rights, Ethics, Arts Council, Historical Preservation, Deaf & Hard of Hearing, Disabilities, Mental Health Advocate, Atomic Energy
why: Each keeps its own director and back office.
Sharing one administrative office could cut overhead without ending any mission.
items.counter: Several are independent by design (Ethics, Human Rights, the advocates), and merging their staff could weaken that independence.
items.next: Total the director and administrative salaries across these offices to size the savings.

why: Pay rose much faster than staff.
The budget jumped 30% in one year.
items.counter: Most of the budget increase is federal highway money for construction, not payroll; winter storms drive overtime.
items.next: Split the budget increase into federal construction funds and state operating costs.

items.counter: Police ranks (sergeant, lieutenant, captain) count as supervisors in a title count, which overstates management. The budget is already falling.
items.next: Use the sworn rank structure, not titles, to judge.

assessment.caveats: Opinion of Rhode Island Hurricane. Based on public payroll and budget records as of the date shown; it does not account for every reorganization, union contract or legal staffing requirement. Agencies are welcome to send corrections.
